findings.title: Insecure TLS version enabled: TLSv1.1
findings.detail: The router accepts TLSv1.1 connections, which is deprecated and vulnerable to downgrade attacks.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLSv1.1 in router TLS configuration. Only TLS 1.2+ should be accepted.

findings.title: TLS 1.3 supported
findings.detail: Good — the router supports the latest TLS version.

findings.title: Vendor default SSL certificate
findings.detail: The router uses a default ASKEY self-signed certificate (CN=askey.com, O=ASKEY, C=CN). This enables MITM attacks as the cert cannot be verified against a trusted CA.
findings.recommendation: Replace the default certificate with a unique cert. Consider DNS-based ACME cert provisioning for home routers.

findings.title: 2048-bit RSA key (minimum)
findings.detail: The certificate uses a 2048-bit RSA key, which is the minimum acceptable size. 4096-bit or EC keys are preferred.
findings.recommendation: Consider upgrading to 4096-bit RSA or ECDSA P-384 for long-term security.

findings.title: No Subject Alternative Name (SAN) in certificate
findings.detail: The certificate lacks SAN extensions, which may cause warnings in modern browsers.
findings.evidence: No SAN found in cert output
findings.recommendation: Regenerate certificate with SAN including the hostname/IP.

findings.title: Multiple security headers missing
findings.detail: The following security headers are not set: X-Frame-Options (clickjacking protection), X-Content-Type-Options (MIME-type sniffing prevention), Content-Security-Policy (XSS/content injection protection), Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS — forces HTTPS), X-XSS-Protection (browser XSS filter). This exposes the router UI to clickjacking, XSS, MIME confusion, and protocol downgrade attacks.
findings.evidence:
X-Frame-Options (clickjacking protection)
X-Content-Type-Options (MIME-type sniffing prevention)
Content-Security-Policy (XSS/content injection protection)
Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS — forces HTTPS)
X-XSS-Protection (browser XSS filter)
findings.recommendation: Configure lighttpd to send: X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self', Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000, X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block.

findings.title: Server version disclosed in HTTP headers
findings.detail: lighttpd/1.4.59 is disclosed via the Server header. Attackers can target known vulnerabilities for this exact version.
findings.recommendation: Set server.tag = '' in lighttpd.conf or use server.tag to show a generic string.

findings.title: Sensitive device info exposed without authentication
findings.detail: The router's unauthenticated info page exposes: WAN IPv4 address: exposed on unauthenticated info page, MAC address: exposed on unauthenticated info page. This aids reconnaissance for targeted attacks including firmware-specific exploits, MAC-based tracking, and WAN IP profiling.
findings.evidence: WAN IP, IPv6, MAC, Serial Number, Model, Firmware Version all visible on /cgi-bin/index.cgi without auth
findings.recommendation: Require authentication to view device information. At minimum, redact WAN IP, MAC, and serial number from unauthenticated pages.

findings.title: connectivity_api accessible without authentication
findings.detail: The /cgi-bin/connectivity_api endpoint returns 'Connected' without requiring authentication. Attackers can determine internet connectivity status.
findings.recommendation: Require authentication for all CGI API endpoints.

findings.title: pods_api accessible without authentication
findings.detail: The /cgi-bin/pods_api endpoint returns data without requiring authentication. Pod serial numbers can be enumerated.
findings.recommendation: Require authentication for all CGI API endpoints.

findings.title: POST /cgi-bin/connectivity_api accepts JSON body
findings.detail: POST to /cgi-bin/connectivity_api with JSON body returned a response (not 411/403/404). May indicate input processing without auth.
findings.recommendation: Validate that POST endpoints require authentication and reject unexpected content types.

findings.title: POST /cgi-bin/pods_api accepts JSON body
findings.detail: POST to /cgi-bin/pods_api with JSON body returned a response (not 411/403/404). May indicate input processing without auth.
findings.recommendation: Validate that POST endpoints require authentication and reject unexpected content types.

findings.title: Path traversal: not exploitable (false positive)
findings.detail: Initial scan flagged path traversal with HTTP 200. Verification shows the response is the router's default info page (index.cgi) or lighttpd 411 error page, not /etc/passwd content. The `/cgi-bin/..;/` path resolves to index.cgi due to lighttpd path normalization, not directory traversal. Non-existent CGI paths return 404 correctly.
findings.evidence: All traversal payloads return generic HTML pages (index.cgi or 411 error), not /etc/passwd content. Non-existent paths return 404.
findings.recommendation: Ensure CGI paths are properly sanitized. Apply input validation on all path components.

findings.title: DNS resolver responds to queries
findings.detail: The router's DNS service resolves external queries. Output: 142.250.176.78
findings.recommendation: If this router is not intended to serve DNS to LAN clients, restrict DNS to internal interfaces only. If serving LAN, ensure it is not accessible from WAN.

findings.title: lighttpd 1.4.59 — potential CVEs applicable
findings.detail: lighttpd 1.4.59 (released ~Dec 2020) may be affected by CVE-2022-37796 (HTTP request smuggling via chunked TE+CL) and other vulnerabilities patched in later versions. The firmware appears to be from Feb 2026 (prod build), but lighttpd version suggests the binary itself may be outdated.
findings.recommendation: Verify if lighttpd patches are included in the firmware build. If not, update to lighttpd 1.4.68+ which addresses known CVEs. Configure server.tag to suppress version disclosure.

findings.title: HTTP/2 enabled
findings.detail: The router supports HTTP/2 (h2 ALPN was seen in nmap results). HTTP/2 multiplexing could be abused for request smuggling if lighttpd's h2 implementation has parsing bugs.
findings.recommendation: Monitor for HTTP/2-specific CVEs in lighttpd.

findings.title: Verify default/weak credentials
findings.detail: Spectrum routers commonly ship with default admin credentials (admin/admin, admin/password, or printed on label). The router uses a CGI-based management interface that requires authentication for changes but exposes info without it.
findings.evidence: Router model SBE1V1K, ASKEY vendor. Common defaults: admin/admin, admin/(serial#), admin/(MAC).
findings.recommendation: 1) Change default admin password. 2) Use a strong, unique password. 3) Disable remote admin access if not needed. 4) Verify no default backdoor accounts exist.

findings.title: Non-standard HTTP methods accepted
findings.detail: The following methods returned non-rejection codes: OPTIONS: 200, CONNECT: 400
findings.recommendation: Disable unnecessary HTTP methods (PUT, DELETE, PATCH) on the router web server.

findings.title: No CORS headers detected
findings.detail: The router does not send CORS headers, which prevents cross-origin JavaScript from interacting with it.
findings.recommendation: Current configuration is acceptable. Maintain absence of permissive CORS headers.
